estimates.narrative: A 2/3 majority is plausible but not assured. Structural amplification and opposition unity lift the odds, while poll divergence and turnout uncertainty keep the probability modest and uncertain.
summary: As of early 2026, polls are mixed with TISZA leading in some surveys and Fidesz in others, yielding no clear path to a guaranteed 2/3 majority.
Hungary's winner-compensation electoral system amplifies seat shares from vote margins, increasing the potential for a 2/3 outcome if a bloc gains votes at the district level.
Opposition consolidation around TISZA raises the anti-Fidesz vote share and could push seats toward 133+ under favorable turnout and translation dynamics.
Historical base-rate shows 2/3 majorities have occurred four times since 1990, indicating the outcome is plausible but not guaranteed.

question: Will any political party or coalition acquire a supermajority in the 2026 Hungarian parliamentary elections?
summary: Ensemble baseline is 60%, but polling dispersion and historical base-rate concerns create caveats that temper confidence in a clear 2/3 path.
Opposition consolidation around TISZA represents a plausible tail risk that could push seat shares toward the 133-seat threshold under favorable turnout and translation into seats.
Hungary's winner-compensation electoral mechanic amplifies margins, which can elevate the chance of a 2/3 outcome if the anti-Fidesz bloc consolidates decisively.
Overall calibration favors a modest upward tilt from the ensemble (to 65%), reflecting upside risk while maintaining recognition of substantial uncertainty.

justification.critique_assessment: Yes—objections about poll dispersion and historical base-rate are valid caveats; opposition consolidation offers a plausible upside tail risk. Together, they justify a cautious, modest upward adjustment rather than a downward shift.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted probability from 0.60 to 0.65 with a 0.55–0.75 range to reflect the upside tail risk from opposition consolidation and the amplification potential of the electoral system, while acknowledging substantial uncertainty.

forecasts.reference-class: Hungarian parliamentary elections under the current mixed-member electoral system (Fidesz–KDNP vs opposition) with historically four two-thirds majorities (2010, 2014, 2018, 2022) achieved through the combination of district/list seats and winner compensation; used as a base-rate for the likelihood of a 133-seat majority.

Real-PR 93 projection indicates the governing coalition would hold about 52.3% of seats, not a two-thirds majority.

Academic analysis argues two-thirds majorities in Hungary have been achieved under the current system and winner compensation; past occurrences include 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022.
Guardian reports TISZA leading in polls and Orbán campaigning; outcome remains uncertain and no guaranteed two-thirds.

2018: Fidesz won a two-thirds majority for the third consecutive term.
2014: Fidesz–KDNP preserved its two-thirds majority.
2022: Fidesz won two-thirds for the fourth time; 2026 election is anticipated.
Analyses how Orbán has secured multiple two-thirds majorities, including mechanisms like winner compensation and near-abroad voting.

Republikon poll (Feb 17, 2026) shows TISZA 47% and Fidesz 39%; projected seats around 107 for TISZA and 82 for Fidesz.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system mechanics (winner-compensation) amplifies margins into seats
causal-factors.rationale: Past analyses show that Hungary's mixed electoral system can convert relatively small vote shares into large seat advantages, contributing to the possibility of a 2/3 majority under favorable conditions.

causal-factors.name: Opposition consolidation around a single slate (e.g., Tisza)
causal-factors.rationale: Polls in some surveys show Tisza leading or closing the gap; stronger coalition coherence could push seat shares toward the 133-seat threshold.

causal-factors.name: Poll dispersion and cross-survey disagreement
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple polls diverge on who leads and by how much, which lowers confidence in any clear path to a 2/3 majority.

causal-factors.name: Seat-projection signals approaching 2/3 for Fidesz in some models
causal-factors.rationale: Certain projection models suggest Fidesz may reach or come close to a two-thirds seat share under current support levels.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate of 2/3 majorities under Hungary's system
causal-factors.rationale: Four of the nine post-1990 elections produced a 2/3 majority, illustrating that the combination of system mechanics and political alignment can yield such outcomes.

causal-factors.name: Uncertain turnout effects and mobilization dynamics
causal-factors.rationale: Turnout levels can shift seat allocations in unpredictable ways, influencing whether any side achieves 2/3 but the direction is not reliably predictable.

causal-factors.name: Structural advantage of the winner-compensation electoral system
causal-factors.rationale: The post-2011 Hungarian system has repeatedly converted sub-50% vote shares into a two-thirds seat majority for the leading bloc (2014, 2018, 2022), indicating a durable structural bias that tends to raise the probability of a 2/3 outcome for whichever bloc dominates district-level wins. ([globalsecurity.org](https://www.globalsecurity.org/military/world/europe/hu-politics-system.htm?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Polling divergence with TISZA ahead or competitive (Feb 2026)
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple credible polls in Jan–Feb 2026 show TISZA leading or closing gap with Fidesz in various measures, suggesting a non-negligible chance that anti-Fidesz seat shares approach or cross the 2/3 threshold under favorable turnout and translation into seats. ([yahoo.com](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/hungarys-tisza-party-leads-pre-090929667.html?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Opposition unity behind TISZA
causal-factors.rationale: Financial Times coverage indicates several opposition groups have quit to back TISZA, increasing anti-Fidesz vote consolidation and potentially improving the anti-regime position. ([ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/85210187-c757-4432-bb57-6b636a669e72?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Vote fragmentation from additional entrants (Our Homeland) entering parliament
causal-factors.rationale: The prospect of Our Homeland crossing the threshold adds fragmentation, which can impede any bloc from achieving a clean, concentrated majority, reducing the odds of a 2/3 outcome for either side. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/02/19/hungarian-polls-split-on-april-election-outcome-as-fidesz-and-tisza-trade-leads?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Turnout and undecided-voter volatility across campaigns
causal-factors.rationale: Divergent polling results and large shares of undecided voters create upside and downside risks to any 2/3 forecast, with momentum swings potentially reshaping seat allocations. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/02/21/parliamentary-election-campaings-begin-in-hungary?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate constraint on 2/3 majorities
causal-factors.rationale: Historically only four of nine post-1990 elections produced 2/3 majorities, showing that such outcomes are the exception rather than the rule under this system. ([robert-schuman.eu](https://www.robert-schuman.eu/en/monitor/1011-the-fidesz-wins-the-2-3-majority-in-the-hungarian-parliament?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Market and model consensus still uncertain about 2/3 prospects
causal-factors.rationale: Divergent polling evidence and seat projections across sources reflect persistent uncertainty, keeping a 2/3 outcome as a non-negligible but unsettled possibility. ([euronews.com](https://www.euronews.com/2026/02/19/hungarian-polls-split-on-april-election-outcome-as-fidesz-and-tisza-trade-leads?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Opposition consolidation around TISZA
causal-factors.rationale: Reports of opposition parties uniting behind TISZA and credible polling showing the anti-Fidesz bloc gaining momentum raise the odds of a large vote share for the challenger.

causal-factors.name: Polling clustering behind TISZA (TISZA ahead in multiple polls)
causal-factors.rationale: Several February 2026 polls place TISZA ahead or competitive (e.g., Republikon 47/39; IDEA 48/38; Závecz 49/39; Publicus 48/39), suggesting a stronger anti-Fidesz position than the anchor implied.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system mechanics (winner compensation) amplifying the leading party's seat share
causal-factors.rationale: Hungary's winner-compensation mechanism can magnify a vote lead into more seats, potentially pushing the leading bloc closer to, or past, a 2/3 threshold if vote margins tilt decisively.

causal-factors.name: Risk of vote fragmentation reducing the likelihood of a 2/3 majority
causal-factors.rationale: Presence of multiple smaller parties in polls and near-threshold results increases fragmentation, making a single party reaching 133 seats less likely.

causal-factors.name: Turnout and mobilization uncertainties
causal-factors.rationale: Turnout swings and undecided-voter mobilization could move outcomes in either direction, but current signals provide limited clarity on net effects.

synthesis: The 60% ensemble hides substantial upside and downside risks: polls are divergent, the historical rarity of 2/3 majorities weighs on confidence, and opposition unity plus the system's mechanics could jointly push toward a 2/3 outcome. A modest upward recalibration to 65% captures this tail risk without overstating likelihood.
